name: IN-08
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Messmer running with large financial edge
No polls or expert ratings; markets price Democratic win at ~3%
model.rationale: This southwestern Indiana seat leans heavily Republican, incumbent Mark Messmer has a roughly four-to-one fundraising advantage, and prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 3% chance. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting movement, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpectedly strong Democratic fundraising could narrow the race, but nothing in the current evidence suggests that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 8th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 18 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Mark Messmer is running for reelection and has raised over $1.1 million, holding a large cash advantage over Democratic challenger Mary Allen, who has raised under $300,000.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance of an upset. The fundamentals, incumbency, and money all point the same direction, making this a safe Republican hold barring unforeseen developments.
